title: Blockmate Ventures chairman: Wyoming site could be 'multi-billion dollar' AI data center play
description:
Blockmate Ventures Inc (TSX-V:MATE, OTCQB:MATEF, FRA:8MH) chairman Domenic Carosa spoke with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about progress on the company's proposed Wyoming data center project, financing discussions, Hivello's expansion into cloud mining and AI products, and a growing pipeline of AI infrastructure projects.

Carosa said Blockmate has submitted its Wyoming zoning application, an important milestone before construction can begin, while also holding discussions with financiers about funding both power infrastructure and construction, including potential equity and debt partners.

The Wyoming site sits opposite a substation and could support a data center of up to 200MW. "200MW in the AI space is quite substantial and at full revenue on the basis that we own the silicon, it would be a multi-billion dollar opportunity," Carosa said, though he stressed the project is being developed in stages - zoning, power, then construction - before Blockmate considers partnering with a neocloud or hyperscaler, operating it directly, or a combination of both.

Carosa also discussed investee Hivello, in which Blockmate holds around 50% on a fully diluted basis. Hivello has launched a Bitcoin cloud mining product, with its next planned product set to leverage AI or GPUs.

Blockmate's infrastructure pipeline is also growing, with three additional projects underway:  some more developed than Wyoming, one already with power up and running, as the company pursues a broader strategy to own, operate and build multiple AI-focused data centers.

title: Big Tech Is Incapable of Solving Its Own Problem, Says Mukunda
description:
Bill Gates, the billionaire co-founder of Microsoft Corp., published a 6,000-word essay on Aug. 26 saying that he would slow the development of artificial intelligence if he could. He elaborated in an interview with the New York Times, saying "in private, people who understand how good this stuff is, and how much better it's getting, they're very worried" but few are raising the issues in public.

The public is already convinced the tech industry can't be trusted with its own creations. Some legal news last week explains why. A bipartisan coalition of 51 attorneys general announced a proposed settlement with Meta Platforms Inc. that obligates the social media company that runs Facebook and Instagram to put tight restrictions on how children use its platforms.

Gautam Mukunda, Lecturer at the Yale School of Management and Bloomberg Opinion contributor, joins Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss.

title: CLARITY stalls, Kalshi heads toward SCOTUS & Wall Street goes onchain
description:
CoinDesk’s The Policy Protocol hosts Rebecca Rettig and Renato Mariotti break down the Ninth Circuit’s ruling against prediction markets like Kalshi, New Jersey’s push to bring the fight before the Supreme Court, and the SEC’s new roundtable on 24/7 trading featuring a roster of TradFi heavyweights.

Then, Katherine Kirkpatrick Bos, Head of Legal at Chainlink, joins the show to discuss 21 global banks planning a joint stablecoin and what it could mean for Circle and Tether, why Kraken’s Bitnomial acquisition could offer a “creative” path to bring Hyperliquid onshore, and the London Stock Exchange’s push to bring its 100 largest companies onchain.

Plus, Kirkpatrick makes the case that legislation remains the only durable way to “future-proof” crypto, while Rebecca and Renato debate whether Congress is entering a post-CLARITY era.

title: GinsGlobal: ITEK up 13% YTD as AI, cybersecurity and defence tech drive rotation
description:
GinsGlobal Index Fund CEO Anthony Ginsberg tells Proactive's Stephen Gunnion that the GinsGlobal Tech Megatrend UCITS ETF (ITEK) fund is up approximately 13% year-to-date and gained more than 5% in August alone, with AI and robotics remaining the top sub-theme at nearly 50% year-to-date gains. Ginsberg said the fund's average price-to-earnings ratio is in the low 20s, which he describes as only a small premium to the S&P 500, arguing that tech is not overvalued at current levels.

Beyond AI and robotics, Ginsberg highlighted cybersecurity, defence tech, blockchain and gene editing as strong performers in August, pointing to a broadening rotation across the tech ecosystem. He cited a global AI infrastructure buildout of close to one trillion dollars in the current year, driven partly by cloud spending and M&A activity, with NVIDIA among the companies making recent acquisitions.

Ginsberg emphasised the fund's equal-weighting approach as a key differentiator, noting that its top 10 holdings represent just over 12% of the portfolio, compared with north of 50% or even 60% for some rival tech funds. The fund holds roughly 60% in US equities and approximately 22% in Asia, including Japan, China and South Korea, with Ginsberg arguing that per-capita cloud spending in Asia already surpasses the US and Europe in some cases.

On the outlook, Ginsberg said tailwinds include a resilient US economy, lower corporate taxes supporting capital expenditure, a weaker US dollar boosting earnings for American tech firms, and the prospect of stable or lower interest rates supporting further M&A. He also flagged anticipated IPOs from Anthropic and OpenAI as likely catalysts for additional corporate spending across the sector.
